newsitem.title: USA: SCE&G restores power to users after storm.
newsitem.headline: SCE&G restores power to users after storm.

text.p: South Carolina Electric & Gas Co (SCE&G) restored service to the 24,000 customers whose power was knocked out Thursday night by Hurricane Fran, the company said Friday.
"We did have 24,000 customers without power, primarily in the coastal area. All services have been restored," said company spokesman Roger Schrumm.
Most of the outages, which began 1800 EDT Thursday, lasted up to 30 minutes as high winds snapped power lines, he said.
"We are in great shape," Schrumm said when asked about the overall status of SCE&G's system, adding that all of the company's active generating stations continued to operate.
The company dispatched repair crews to aid Carolina Power & Light Co and Virginia Power, whose systems were severely hit by the hurricane.
On Friday, Fran was downgraded to a tropical storm as it continued to lose strength along its path through Virginia and West Virginia.
SCE&G, a subsidiary of SCANA Corp, serves 500,000 electric and 250,000 natural gas customers in the middle and southern portions of South Carolina.
